A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 16-page LAMP study, including supplementary material and references. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original trajectory evaluations, ablations, generated-video examples and a 16-participant user study, including supplementary experimental results.

after.justification: v4 retains the original trajectory evaluations, ablations, generated-video examples, user study and supplementary results.

M1.justification: The LLM motion planner, four DSL primitives, deterministic trajectory conversion and video-conditioning procedure are identical, including supplementary specifications.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the procedural dataset, DataDoP, ET and CameraBench-based evaluations, alongside the same supplementary multi-object and long-horizon scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1, 2, 5 and 6. The video study retains the same Wan 2.1, GPT-DSL and GPT-Traj baselines.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, training configurations and user-study procedures are unchanged. The direct-trajectory Revised F1-Score protocol described in supplementary Section 2.1 already appears in v3.

E4.justification: The DSL-versus-trajectory ablation, supplementary training and caption analyses, qualitative cases and DSL failure analysis are identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained, including Tables 1–6, the user-study findings in Figure 6 and the supplementary 0.11% DSL failure rate.

T1.justification: Equation (1), mathematical descriptions and DSL definitions are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same joint object/camera planning novelty claim, DSL/data/interface contributions and controllability claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of DSL advantages and generalization remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning motion diversity, multi-object coordination and video adherence.

D1.justification: DSL parameter tables, model and hardware details, runtime disclosures and project/code access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 39 works are cited with unchanged research positioning. References [5] and [22] receive author-metadata edits, but their titles, publication details and cited roles remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Reference [5] changes Norman Christie to Marc Christie and places Patrick Olivier before Jean-Marie Normand. Reference [22] changes Matheus Lino and Norman Christie to Christophe Lino and Marc Christie. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; other prose and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions and placements are unchanged; pages 2–14 render identically. The stamp and reference-author edits preserve the existing page layout.

improvement.justification: The differences are confined to author metadata in references [5] and [22] and the arXiv stamp. These limited editorial edits leave the scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and presentation materially unchanged.
